_about: A350F (Airbus's A350-1000F), from Airbus AC A350 (Jul 01/26) 2-2-0 General Aircraft Dimensions, A350-1000F sheets 1 (side, front: page index 53) and 2 (plan: page index 54). Shaded pictures: layers.py --mode lines, line centres. Drawn 4.7% larger than the A350-1000's sheets: the side at scale 8, 42.24 px a meter (its door 1 and aft bulk cargo door against the A350-1000's less the plug; the printed 69.07 m then falls on its tail cone); the plan at 7.429 (the A350-1000's), the front at 8.1884 (its span and nacelles 2.25% larger than the A350-1000's front at scale 8), both to the side's scale. The A350-1000's points moved by one plug out (3.17 m ahead of the wing: the printed main gear 29.31 m against 32.48 m, nose-to-engine 22.61 m against 25.78 m, length 69.07 m against 72.25 m) and the sheet's scale (plug.py), the parts laid on by best fit, then snapped (a35k-freighter/*.anchors.json). The main-deck cargo door is a cargo door; the four small windows the sheet draws at the cabin's window row are kept.

sources.title: Airbus, A350 Aircraft Characteristics: Airport and Maintenance Planning (Jul 01/26), 2-2-0 General Aircraft Dimensions, A350-1000F sheets 1 and 2
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the side, plan and front views (tools/trace/a35k-freighter/), starting from the A350-1000's points moved by the one fuselage plug out (3.17 m ahead of the wing, from the sheet's printed figures); the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. Shaded picture sheets of about 42 pixels a meter: outlines good to about 3 cm. The main-deck cargo door behind the wing is drawn as a cargo door; the cockpit panes are the A350-1000's (the same nose). The sheet draws four small windows at the cabin's window row (behind door 1, two ahead of the cargo door, one aft of it); the shape keeps them. The plan draws the tailplane wider than its printed 18.79 m span, as on the A350-900's and A350-1000's sheets; the shape keeps the plan's.
